verses.sanskrit: या देवी सर्वभूतेषु चेतनेत्यभिधीयते | नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमस्तस्यै नमो नमः ||
verses.transliteration: yā devī sarvabhūteṣu cetanetyabhidhīyate | namastasyai namastasyai namastasyai namo namaḥ ||
verses.translation: To the Devi who dwells in all beings as consciousness — salutations again and again and again.
verses.hindi: जो देवी सभी प्राणियों में चेतना-रूप में निवास करती हैं — उन्हें बार-बार नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार, बार-बार नमस्कार।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata's most striking declaration: the Divine Mother is not an external deity to be worshipped at a distance — she IS the consciousness within every being. To encounter any conscious being — human, animal, plant — is to encounter the Devi. Worship is not ritual alone; it is recognition. Seeing consciousness in another and responding with reverence IS Devi puja.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं हि वषट्कारस्वरात्मिका | सुधा त्वमक्षरे नित्ये त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkārasvarātmikā | sudhā tvamakṣare nitye tridhā mātrātmikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.
verses.hindi: तुम स्वाहा हो, तुम स्वधा हो, तुम ही वषट् स्वर-स्वरूपा हो। तुम सुधा (अमृत) हो, नित्य और अक्षर, त्रिमात्रा (OM की तीन मात्रा) रूप में स्थित।
verses.commentary: The Devi is identified with every sacred utterance and act: svaha (the offering to gods in fire), svadha (the offering to ancestors), vashat (the potent sound in Vedic rituals), and finally — sudha (nectar, immortality). She is the sacred act itself, not just its recipient. The Divine Mother is not above the world receiving offerings — she IS the offering, the giving, the act of generosity itself.

verses.sanskrit: वने गत्वा तपस्तप्तं वासुदेवेन दुष्करम् । विष्णोरंशावतारेण शिवस्याराधनं कृतम् ||
verses.transliteration: vane gatvā tapas taptaṃ vāsudevena duṣkaram | viṣṇor aṃśāvatāreṇa śivasyārādhanaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.
verses.hindi: वन में जाकर वासुदेव ने कठिन तप किया; विष्णु-अंशावतार होते हुए भी उन्होंने शिव की आराधना की।
verses.commentary: This verse is striking because it refuses sectarian simplicity. Krishna, understood as Vishnu's manifestation, worships Shiva. The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत | अथ कस्यायं माययो सृष्टः सङ्घातः प्रपञ्चः ||
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta | atha kasyāyaṃ māyayo sṛṣṭaḥ saṅghātaḥ prapañcaḥ ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Brahman — calm, one should meditate on That. From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में ब्रह्म है — शांत होकर उसी का उपासन करो। फिर यह माया से सृष्ट संघात, यह प्रपंच, किसका है?
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata echoes the Chandogya Upanishad's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" while adding a crucial twist. It affirms non-dual Brahman as the substance of all — but then asks the penetrating question: "From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?" The Devi Bhagavata's answer: from Mahamaya, the great illusion, which is herself. The Devi is both the reality (Brahman) and the power of illusion (Maya). This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.sanskrit: सूत उवाच । प्रणम्य परमां शक्तिं चतुर्वर्गप्रदायिनीम् । आदिशक्तिं वदिष्यामि कथां पौराणिकीं शुभाम् ||
verses.transliteration: sūta uvāca | praṇamya paramāṃ śaktiṃ caturvargapradāyinīm | ādiśaktiṃ vadiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ śubhām ||
verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.
verses.hindi: सूत ने कहा: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष देने वाली परम शक्ति को प्रणाम कर मैं आदि शक्ति की शुभ पुराण-कथा कहूँगा।
verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.sanskrit: सा च ब्रह्मस्वरूपा च नित्या सा च सनातनी । यथाऽऽत्मा च तथा शक्तिर्यथाग्नौ दाहिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: sā ca brahmasvarūpā ca nityā sā ca sanātanī | yathātmā ca tathā śaktir yathāgnau dāhikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: She is of the nature of Brahman; she is eternal and ancient. As the Self is, so is Shakti, just as burning power abides in fire.
verses.hindi: वह ब्रह्मस्वरूपा है, नित्य और सनातनी है। जैसे आत्मा है वैसे ही शक्ति है, जैसे अग्नि में दाहक शक्ति स्थित रहती है।
verses.commentary: Skandha 9 gives one of the clearest Shakta metaphors: Shakti is to Brahman as burning power is to fire. You cannot separate fire from its capacity to burn, nor consciousness from its power to manifest. The verse dissolves the idea that Shakti is secondary. She is Brahman's own living potency.

verses.sanskrit: जगतस्तत्त्वमित्येव देवी प्रोक्ता मयापि हि । ऋषिभिर्देवगन्धर्वैरन्यैश्चापि मनीषिभिः ||
verses.transliteration: jagatas tattvam ity eva devī proktā mayāpi hi | ṛṣibhir devagandharvair anyaiś cāpi manīṣibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.
verses.hindi: देवी को ही जगत् का तत्त्व कहा गया है — मेरे द्वारा, ऋषियों द्वारा, देवों-गंधर्वों द्वारा और अन्य मनीषियों द्वारा भी।
verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. Devi is named as the principle that makes the universe intelligible. The text asks us to see cosmology not as a map of places only, but as a map of dependence on the Mother.

verses.sanskrit: देवी सर्वभूतानां हृदये संनिविष्टा | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: देवी सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that Devi dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Devi is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.sanskrit: शक्तिश्च शिवश्च एकैव भिन्ना नास्ति कदाचन | यो शक्तिशिवयोरेकं जानाति स परां गतिम् ||
verses.transliteration: śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva bhinna nāsti kadācana | yo śaktiśivayorekaṃ jānāti sa parāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: Shakti and Shiva are one — there is no separation ever. He who knows the unity of Shakti and Shiva attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: शक्ति और शिव एक हैं — कभी भी भेद नहीं। जो शक्ति-शिव की एकता जानता है, वह परम गति प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata teaches the supreme truth of Shakti-Shiva unity. Shakti is not merely Shiva's consort but the embodiment of energy — the divine power that is inseparable from Shiva. "Śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva" — Shakti and Shiva are one — is the recognition that consciousness (Shiva) and energy (Shakti) are one reality. This is not philosophical abstraction but the recognition that the divine is both the witnessing consciousness and the active power of manifestation.

verses.sanskrit: देवी साक्षात् परं ब्रह्म निर्गुणा निश्चला शुधा | योगिनां हृदये नित्यं देवी भवति साक्षात् ||
verses.transliteration: devī sākṣāt paraṃ brahma nirguṇā niścalā śudhā | yogināṃ hṛdaye nityaṃ devī bhavati sākṣāt ||
verses.translation: Devi is indeed the supreme Brahman — without qualities, unmoving, pure. In the hearts of yogins, Devi is indeed present.
verses.hindi: देवी साक्षात् परम ब्रह्म हैं — निर्गुण, निश्चल, शुद्ध। योगियों के हृदय में देवी साक्षात् विराजमान हैं।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata identifies Devi with the supreme Brahman — nirguna (without qualities), nishcala (unmoving), shuddha (pure). This is the non-dual teaching: Devi is not a deity among deities but the absolute reality itself. The verse then states that this absolute reality is present in the hearts of yogins — not as a distant abstraction but as immediate presence. The yogin's heart is the location where the absolute becomes accessible.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं देवी न भूतं न भविष्यति | सा एव सर्वशक्त्याढ्या सर्वकारणकारणम् ||
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati | sā eva sarvaśaktyāḍhyā sarvakāraṇakāraṇam ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Devi — what was not, what will not be. She alone is endowed with all powers, the cause of all causes.
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में देवी है — जो नहीं था, जो नहीं होगा। वही सभी शक्तियों से युक्त, सभी कारणों का कारण है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that all existence is Devi — past, present, and future. "Sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī" — all this is indeed Devi. The verse states that Devi is endowed with all powers and is the cause of all causes. This is the ultimate non-dual teaching: there is nothing that is not Devi. The world is not separate from the divine; the world IS the divine in manifestation.

verses.translation: If Shiva is without Shakti, what can the great lord do? Only when Brahma is joined with Shakti does he create.
verses.hindi: यदि शिव शक्तिहीन हों तो महेश्वर क्या करेंगे? और जब ब्रह्म शक्ति से युक्त होते हैं, तभी वे सृष्टि करते हैं।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata's radical claim: all the great gods — Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu — are powerless without Shakti (the feminine power/energy). verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.

verses.commentary: The Devi is identified with every sacred utterance and act: svaha (the offering to gods in fire), svadha (the offering to ancestors), vashat (the potent sound in Vedic rituals), and finally — sudha (nectar, immortality). verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.

Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.
verses.hindi: सूत ने कहा: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष देने वाली परम शक्ति को प्रणाम कर मैं आदि शक्ति की शुभ पुराण-कथा कहूँगा।
verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.translation: Devi is indeed the supreme Brahman — without qualities, unmoving, pure. In the hearts of yogins, Devi is indeed present.
verses.hindi: देवी साक्षात् परम ब्रह्म हैं — निर्गुण, निश्चल, शुद्ध। योगियों के हृदय में देवी साक्षात् विराजमान हैं।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata identifies Devi with the supreme Brahman — nirguna (without qualities), nishcala (unmoving), shuddha (pure). This is the non-dual teaching: Devi is not a deity among deities but the absolute reality itself. The verse then states that this absolute reality is present in the hearts of yogins — not as a distant abstraction but as immediate presence. The yogin's heart is the location where the absolute becomes accessible.

verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati | sā eva sarvaśaktyāḍhyā sarvakāraṇakāraṇam ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Devi — what was not, what will not be. She alone is endowed with all powers, the cause of all causes.
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में देवी है — जो नहीं था, जो नहीं होगा। वही सभी शक्तियों से युक्त, सभी कारणों का कारण है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that all existence is Devi — past, present, and future. "Sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī" — all this is indeed Devi. The verse states that Devi is endowed with all powers and is the cause of all causes. This is the ultimate non-dual teaching: there is nothing that is not Devi. The world is not separate from the divine; the world IS the divine in manifestation.

verses.sanskrit: शूरसेनसुतः श्रीमान्वसुदेवः प्रतापवान् । श्रुतं मया हरिर्यस्य पुत्रभावमवाप्तवान् ||
verses.transliteration: śūrasenasutaḥ śrīmān vasudevaḥ pratāpavān | śrutaṃ mayā harir yasya putrabhāvam avāptavān ||
verses.translation: I have heard of the glorious and mighty Vasudeva, son of Shurasena, to whom Hari came in the form of a son.
verses.hindi: मैंने शूरसेन-पुत्र, श्रीमान् और प्रतापी वसुदेव के विषय में सुना है, जिनके यहाँ हरि पुत्ररूप में प्रकट हुए।
verses.commentary: Skandha 4 opens Krishna's birth story by naming Vasudeva before the miracle. The divine descent enters through a human parent, a lineage, and a vulnerable family. In the Shakta reading, even an avatar is not abstract; the Mother's power works through birth, kinship, protection, and the fragile conditions of embodied life.

verses.sanskrit: वने गत्वा तपस्तप्तं वासुदेवेन दुष्करम् । विष्णोरंशावतारेण शिवस्याराधनं कृतम् ||
verses.transliteration: vane gatvā tapas taptaṃ vāsudevena duṣkaram | viṣṇor aṃśāvatāreṇa śivasyārādhanaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.
verses.hindi: वन में जाकर वासुदेव ने कठिन तप किया; विष्णु-अंशावतार होते हुए भी उन्होंने शिव की आराधना की।
verses.commentary: This verse is striking because it refuses sectarian simplicity. Krishna, understood as Vishnu's manifestation, worships Shiva. The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत | अथ कस्यायं माययो सृष्टः सङ्घातः प्रपञ्चः ||
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta | atha kasyāyaṃ māyayo sṛṣṭaḥ saṅghātaḥ prapañcaḥ ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Brahman — calm, one should meditate on That. From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में ब्रह्म है — शांत होकर उसी का उपासन करो। फिर यह माया से सृष्ट संघात, यह प्रपंच, किसका है?
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata echoes the Chandogya Upanishad's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" while adding a crucial twist. It affirms non-dual Brahman as the substance of all — but then asks the penetrating question: "From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?" The Devi Bhagavata's answer: from Mahamaya, the great illusion, which is herself. The Devi is both the reality (Brahman) and the power of illusion (Maya). This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.sanskrit: सूत उवाच । प्रणम्य परमां शक्तिं चतुर्वर्गप्रदायिनीम् । आदिशक्तिं वदिष्यामि कथां पौराणिकीं शुभाम् ||
verses.transliteration: sūta uvāca | praṇamya paramāṃ śaktiṃ caturvargapradāyinīm | ādiśaktiṃ vadiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ śubhām ||
verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.
verses.hindi: सूत ने कहा: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष देने वाली परम शक्ति को प्रणाम कर मैं आदि शक्ति की शुभ पुराण-कथा कहूँगा।
verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.sanskrit: सा च ब्रह्मस्वरूपा च नित्या सा च सनातनी । यथाऽऽत्मा च तथा शक्तिर्यथाग्नौ दाहिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: sā ca brahmasvarūpā ca nityā sā ca sanātanī | yathātmā ca tathā śaktir yathāgnau dāhikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: She is of the nature of Brahman; she is eternal and ancient. As the Self is, so is Shakti, just as burning power abides in fire.
verses.hindi: वह ब्रह्मस्वरूपा है, नित्य और सनातनी है। जैसे आत्मा है वैसे ही शक्ति है, जैसे अग्नि में दाहक शक्ति स्थित रहती है।
verses.commentary: Skandha 9 gives one of the clearest Shakta metaphors: Shakti is to Brahman as burning power is to fire. You cannot separate fire from its capacity to burn, nor consciousness from its power to manifest. The verse dissolves the idea that Shakti is secondary. She is Brahman's own living potency.

verses.sanskrit: जगतस्तत्त्वमित्येव देवी प्रोक्ता मयापि हि । ऋषिभिर्देवगन्धर्वैरन्यैश्चापि मनीषिभिः ||
verses.transliteration: jagatas tattvam ity eva devī proktā mayāpi hi | ṛṣibhir devagandharvair anyaiś cāpi manīṣibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.
verses.hindi: देवी को ही जगत् का तत्त्व कहा गया है — मेरे द्वारा, ऋषियों द्वारा, देवों-गंधर्वों द्वारा और अन्य मनीषियों द्वारा भी।
verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. Devi is named as the principle that makes the universe intelligible. The text asks us to see cosmology not as a map of places only, but as a map of dependence on the Mother.

verses.sanskrit: देवी सर्वभूतानां हृदये संनिविष्टा | यो जानाति स पश्यति यो न जानाति न पश्यति ||
verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: देवी सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that Devi dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Devi is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.sanskrit: शक्तिश्च शिवश्च एकैव भिन्ना नास्ति कदाचन | यो शक्तिशिवयोरेकं जानाति स परां गतिम् ||
verses.transliteration: śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva bhinna nāsti kadācana | yo śaktiśivayorekaṃ jānāti sa parāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: Shakti and Shiva are one — there is no separation ever. He who knows the unity of Shakti and Shiva attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: शक्ति और शिव एक हैं — कभी भी भेद नहीं। जो शक्ति-शिव की एकता जानता है, वह परम गति प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata teaches the supreme truth of Shakti-Shiva unity. Shakti is not merely Shiva's consort but the embodiment of energy — the divine power that is inseparable from Shiva. "Śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva" — Shakti and Shiva are one — is the recognition that consciousness (Shiva) and energy (Shakti) are one reality. This is not philosophical abstraction but the recognition that the divine is both the witnessing consciousness and the active power of manifestation.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं हि वषट्कारस्वरात्मिका | सुधा त्वमक्षरे नित्ये त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkārasvarātmikā | sudhā tvamakṣare nitye tridhā mātrātmikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.
verses.hindi: तुम स्वाहा हो, तुम स्वधा हो, तुम ही वषट् स्वर-स्वरूपा हो। तुम सुधा (अमृत) हो, नित्य और अक्षर, त्रिमात्रा (OM की तीन मात्रा) रूप में स्थित।
verses.commentary: The Devi is identified with every sacred utterance and act: svaha (the offering to gods in fire), svadha (the offering to ancestors), vashat (the potent sound in Vedic rituals), and finally — sudha (nectar, immortality). She is the sacred act itself, not just its recipient. The Divine Mother is not above the world receiving offerings — she IS the offering, the giving, the act of generosity itself.

verses.translation: We wish to ask you again about an auspicious Puranic story, delightful, famous, destroying sin, and spoken of even in the Veda.

verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.

The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.translation: All this is indeed Brahman — calm, one should meditate on That. From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?

verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata echoes the Chandogya Upanishad's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" while adding a crucial twist. This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.hindi: देवी साक्षात् परम ब्रह्म हैं — निर्गुण, निश्चल, शुद्ध। योगियों के हृदय में देवी साक्षात् विराजमान हैं।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata identifies Devi with the supreme Brahman — nirguna (without qualities), nishcala (unmoving), shuddha (pure). This is the non-dual teaching: Devi is not a deity among deities but the absolute reality itself. The verse then states that this absolute reality is present in the hearts of yogins — not as a distant abstraction but as immediate presence. The yogin's heart is the location where the absolute becomes accessible.

verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati | sā eva sarvaśaktyāḍhyā sarvakāraṇakāraṇam ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Devi — what was not, what will not be. She alone is endowed with all powers, the cause of all causes.
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में देवी है — जो नहीं था, जो नहीं होगा। वही सभी शक्तियों से युक्त, सभी कारणों का कारण है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that all existence is Devi — past, present, and future. "Sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ devī" — all this is indeed Devi. The verse states that Devi is endowed with all powers and is the cause of all causes. This is the ultimate non-dual teaching: there is nothing that is not Devi. The world is not separate from the divine; the world IS the divine in manifestation.

verses.sanskrit: अहमेवाससं पूर्वं नान्यत् किञ्चिच्च बालकाः | तदात्मरूपं चित्संवित्परं ब्रह्माद्वयं विभु ||
verses.transliteration: ahamevāsasaṃ pūrvaṃ nānyat kiñcicca bālakāḥ | tadātmarūpaṃ citsaṃvitparaṃ brahmādvayaṃ vibhu ||
verses.translation: I alone existed in the beginning, O children — nothing else whatsoever. That, my own form, is pure consciousness-awareness — the supreme, non-dual, all-pervading Brahman.
verses.hindi: हे बालकों! प्रारंभ में मैं ही थी; और कुछ नहीं था। वही मेरा स्वरूप — चित्-संवित्, परम अद्वय ब्रह्म, सर्वव्यापी।
verses.commentary: The Devi Gita's declaration: "I alone existed." This is identical in form to the Vedantic mahavakya, but spoken by the feminine. The Divine Mother is not subordinate to a male Brahman; she IS Brahman in her own voice. Pure consciousness-awareness (chit-samvit), non-dual (advaya), all-pervading (vibhu) — these are the qualifiers the Upanishads use for Brahman, and here they all belong to the Devi. The Shakta tradition restores the feminine to the highest metaphysical position.

verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta | atha kasyāyaṃ māyayo sṛṣṭaḥ saṅghātaḥ prapañcaḥ ||

This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: देवी सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that Devi dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Devi is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.transliteration: śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva bhinna nāsti kadācana | yo śaktiśivayorekaṃ jānāti sa parāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: Shakti and Shiva are one — there is no separation ever. He who knows the unity of Shakti and Shiva attains the supreme state.
verses.hindi: शक्ति और शिव एक हैं — कभी भी भेद नहीं। जो शक्ति-शिव की एकता जानता है, वह परम गति प्राप्त करता है।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata teaches the supreme truth of Shakti-Shiva unity. Shakti is not merely Shiva's consort but the embodiment of energy — the divine power that is inseparable from Shiva. "Śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva" — Shakti and Shiva are one — is the recognition that consciousness (Shiva) and energy (Shakti) are one reality. This is not philosophical abstraction but the recognition that the divine is both the witnessing consciousness and the active power of manifestation.

verses.sanskrit: जगतस्तत्त्वमित्येव देवी प्रोक्ता मयापि हि । ऋषिभिर्देवगन्धर्वैरन्यैश्चापि मनीषिभिः ||
verses.transliteration: jagatas tattvam ity eva devī proktā mayāpi hi | ṛṣibhir devagandharvair anyaiś cāpi manīṣibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.
verses.hindi: देवी को ही जगत् का तत्त्व कहा गया है — मेरे द्वारा, ऋषियों द्वारा, देवों-गंधर्वों द्वारा और अन्य मनीषियों द्वारा भी।
verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. Devi is named as the principle that makes the universe intelligible. The text asks us to see cosmology not as a map of places only, but as a map of dependence on the Mother.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं हि वषट्कारस्वरात्मिका | सुधा त्वमक्षरे नित्ये त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkārasvarātmikā | sudhā tvamakṣare nitye tridhā mātrātmikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.
verses.hindi: तुम स्वाहा हो, तुम स्वधा हो, तुम ही वषट् स्वर-स्वरूपा हो। तुम सुधा (अमृत) हो, नित्य और अक्षर, त्रिमात्रा (OM की तीन मात्रा) रूप में स्थित।
verses.commentary: The Devi is identified with every sacred utterance and act: svaha (the offering to gods in fire), svadha (the offering to ancestors), vashat (the potent sound in Vedic rituals), and finally — sudha (nectar, immortality). She is the sacred act itself, not just its recipient. The Divine Mother is not above the world receiving offerings — she IS the offering, the giving, the act of generosity itself.

verses.sanskrit: वने गत्वा तपस्तप्तं वासुदेवेन दुष्करम् । विष्णोरंशावतारेण शिवस्याराधनं कृतम् ||
verses.transliteration: vane gatvā tapas taptaṃ vāsudevena duṣkaram | viṣṇor aṃśāvatāreṇa śivasyārādhanaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.
verses.hindi: वन में जाकर वासुदेव ने कठिन तप किया; विष्णु-अंशावतार होते हुए भी उन्होंने शिव की आराधना की।
verses.commentary: This verse is striking because it refuses sectarian simplicity. Krishna, understood as Vishnu's manifestation, worships Shiva. The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.transliteration: sūta uvāca | praṇamya paramāṃ śaktiṃ caturvargapradāyinīm | ādiśaktiṃ vadiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ śubhām ||
verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.
verses.hindi: सूत ने कहा: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष देने वाली परम शक्ति को प्रणाम कर मैं आदि शक्ति की शुभ पुराण-कथा कहूँगा।
verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.sanskrit: सा च ब्रह्मस्वरूपा च नित्या सा च सनातनी । यथाऽऽत्मा च तथा शक्तिर्यथाग्नौ दाहिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: sā ca brahmasvarūpā ca nityā sā ca sanātanī | yathātmā ca tathā śaktir yathāgnau dāhikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: She is of the nature of Brahman; she is eternal and ancient. As the Self is, so is Shakti, just as burning power abides in fire.
verses.hindi: वह ब्रह्मस्वरूपा है, नित्य और सनातनी है। जैसे आत्मा है वैसे ही शक्ति है, जैसे अग्नि में दाहक शक्ति स्थित रहती है।
verses.commentary: Skandha 9 gives one of the clearest Shakta metaphors: Shakti is to Brahman as burning power is to fire. You cannot separate fire from its capacity to burn, nor consciousness from its power to manifest. The verse dissolves the idea that Shakti is secondary. She is Brahman's own living potency.

verses.transliteration: sā ca brahmasvarūpā ca nityā sā ca sanātanī | yathātmā ca tathā śaktir yathāgnau dāhikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: She is of the nature of Brahman; she is eternal and ancient. As the Self is, so is Shakti, just as burning power abides in fire.

verses.transliteration: vane gatvā tapas taptaṃ vāsudevena duṣkaram | viṣṇor aṃśāvatāreṇa śivasyārādhanaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.
verses.hindi: वन में जाकर वासुदेव ने कठिन तप किया; विष्णु-अंशावतार होते हुए भी उन्होंने शिव की आराधना की।
verses.commentary: This verse is striking because it refuses sectarian simplicity. Krishna, understood as Vishnu's manifestation, worships Shiva. The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta | atha kasyāyaṃ māyayo sṛṣṭaḥ saṅghātaḥ prapañcaḥ ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Brahman — calm, one should meditate on That. From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में ब्रह्म है — शांत होकर उसी का उपासन करो। फिर यह माया से सृष्ट संघात, यह प्रपंच, किसका है?
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata echoes the Chandogya Upanishad's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" while adding a crucial twist. It affirms non-dual Brahman as the substance of all — but then asks the penetrating question: "From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?" The Devi Bhagavata's answer: from Mahamaya, the great illusion, which is herself. The Devi is both the reality (Brahman) and the power of illusion (Maya). This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.

verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.transliteration: jagatas tattvam ity eva devī proktā mayāpi hi | ṛṣibhir devagandharvair anyaiś cāpi manīṣibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.

verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. Devi is named as the principle that makes the universe intelligible. The text asks us to see cosmology not as a map of places only, but as a map of dependence on the Mother.

verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: देवी सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that Devi dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Devi is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.translation: O honored and worshipful bearer of the world, auspicious among all that is auspicious, by the glance of your eye the lotus-born Brahma creates the universe.

verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.

The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.

verses.transliteration: śaktiśca śivaśca ekaiva bhinna nāsti kadācana | yo śaktiśivayorekaṃ jānāti sa parāṃ gatim ||
verses.translation: Shakti and Shiva are one — there is no separation ever. He who knows the unity of Shakti and Shiva attains the supreme state.

The verse then states that this absolute reality is present in the hearts of yogins — not as a distant abstraction but as immediate presence. The yogin's heart is the location where the absolute becomes accessible.

verses.commentary: Skandha 11 turns devotion into daily conduct. The Devi is pleased not only by praise but by achara — embodied discipline, ethical habit, and regular practice. The verse links conduct to life, community, food, and purification because behavior is the bridge between belief and consequence.

verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.

verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.

verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. verses.transliteration: nyāsān karotu vā mā vā gāyatrīm eva cābhyaset | dhyātvā nirvyājayā vṛttyā saccidānandarūpiṇīm ||
verses.translation: Whether one performs the nyasas or not, one should practice Gayatri alone, meditating with an unpretending disposition on her whose form is existence, consciousness, and bliss.

verses.commentary: The final skandha simplifies practice. Ritual details have value, but the heart of the teaching is steady Gayatri practice with sincerity. The Devi is contemplated as sat-cit-ananda — existence, consciousness, and bliss — so mantra becomes a direct return to the nature of reality.

verses.sanskrit: त्वं स्वाहा त्वं स्वधा त्वं हि वषट्कारस्वरात्मिका | सुधा त्वमक्षरे नित्ये त्रिधा मात्रात्मिका स्थिता ||
verses.transliteration: tvaṃ svāhā tvaṃ svadhā tvaṃ hi vaṣaṭkārasvarātmikā | sudhā tvamakṣare nitye tridhā mātrātmikā sthitā ||
verses.translation: You are Svaha (the sacred offering), you are Svadha (the ancestral offering), you are the essence of the Vashat sound; you are Sudha (nectar), eternal and imperishable, dwelling in three measures.
verses.hindi: तुम स्वाहा हो, तुम स्वधा हो, तुम ही वषट् स्वर-स्वरूपा हो। तुम सुधा (अमृत) हो, नित्य और अक्षर, त्रिमात्रा (OM की तीन मात्रा) रूप में स्थित।
verses.commentary: The Devi is identified with every sacred utterance and act: svaha (the offering to gods in fire), svadha (the offering to ancestors), vashat (the potent sound in Vedic rituals), and finally — sudha (nectar, immortality). She is the sacred act itself, not just its recipient. The Divine Mother is not above the world receiving offerings — she IS the offering, the giving, the act of generosity itself.

verses.transliteration: vane gatvā tapas taptaṃ vāsudevena duṣkaram | viṣṇor aṃśāvatāreṇa śivasyārādhanaṃ kṛtam ||
verses.translation: Going to the forest, Vasudeva performed difficult austerity; as an incarnation of Vishnu, he worshipped Shiva.
verses.hindi: वन में जाकर वासुदेव ने कठिन तप किया; विष्णु-अंशावतार होते हुए भी उन्होंने शिव की आराधना की।
verses.commentary: This verse is striking because it refuses sectarian simplicity. Krishna, understood as Vishnu's manifestation, worships Shiva. The Devi Bhagavata uses such scenes to show that divine forms are not rivals but interdependent expressions of one sacred reality. Humility before another form of the divine is not weakness; it is spiritual maturity.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म तज्जलानिति शान्त उपासीत | अथ कस्यायं माययो सृष्टः सङ्घातः प्रपञ्चः ||
verses.transliteration: sarvaṃ khalvidaṃ brahma tajjalāniti śānta upāsīta | atha kasyāyaṃ māyayo sṛṣṭaḥ saṅghātaḥ prapañcaḥ ||
verses.translation: All this is indeed Brahman — calm, one should meditate on That. From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?
verses.hindi: सब कुछ वास्तव में ब्रह्म है — शांत होकर उसी का उपासन करो। फिर यह माया से सृष्ट संघात, यह प्रपंच, किसका है?
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata echoes the Chandogya Upanishad's "sarvam khalvidam brahma" while adding a crucial twist. It affirms non-dual Brahman as the substance of all — but then asks the penetrating question: "From what was this created illusion, this manifold world?" The Devi Bhagavata's answer: from Mahamaya, the great illusion, which is herself. The Devi is both the reality (Brahman) and the power of illusion (Maya). This is the Shakta non-duality: the one reality has two faces — the face of truth (sat) and the face of creative illusion (maya). Both are the Devi.

verses.transliteration: sūta uvāca | praṇamya paramāṃ śaktiṃ caturvargapradāyinīm | ādiśaktiṃ vadiṣyāmi kathāṃ paurāṇikīṃ śubhām ||
verses.translation: Suta said: Having bowed to the supreme Shakti, the giver of the four aims of life, I shall tell the auspicious ancient story of Adi Shakti.
verses.hindi: सूत ने कहा: धर्म, अर्थ, काम और मोक्ष देने वाली परम शक्ति को प्रणाम कर मैं आदि शक्ति की शुभ पुराण-कथा कहूँगा।
verses.commentary: Skandha 2 begins by placing the whole narrative under the sovereignty of Adi Shakti. The four purusharthas — dharma, artha, kama, and moksha — are not treated as separate human pursuits but as gifts flowing from the same primordial power. The story of Bharata, Vyasa, Satyavati, and the royal lineages is therefore not merely dynastic history; it is the movement of Shakti through family, duty, memory, and destiny.

verses.transliteration: jagatas tattvam ity eva devī proktā mayāpi hi | ṛṣibhir devagandharvair anyaiś cāpi manīṣibhiḥ ||
verses.translation: The Devi is indeed declared to be the very principle of the universe — by me, by the seers, by the gods and gandharvas, and by other wise ones.
verses.hindi: देवी को ही जगत् का तत्त्व कहा गया है — मेरे द्वारा, ऋषियों द्वारा, देवों-गंधर्वों द्वारा और अन्य मनीषियों द्वारा भी।
verses.commentary: Skandha 8 moves from cosmography to metaphysics: the islands, worlds, and cosmic regions are not dead geography but expressions of one underlying tattva. Devi is named as the principle that makes the universe intelligible. The text asks us to see cosmology not as a map of places only, but as a map of dependence on the Mother.

verses.transliteration: devī sarvabhūtānāṃ hṛdaye saṃniviṣṭā | yo jānāti sa paśyati yo na jānāti na paśyati ||
verses.translation: Devi dwells in the heart of all beings. He who knows, sees; he who does not know, does not see.
verses.hindi: देवी सभी प्राणियों के हृदय में निवास करती हैं। जो जानता है, वह देखता है; जो नहीं जानता, वह नहीं देखता।
verses.commentary: The Devi Bhagavata declares that Devi dwells in the heart of all beings — not in distant heavens but in the innermost center of every living being. The verse then states the paradox of recognition: knowledge is seeing, ignorance is blindness. Devi is equally present in all hearts, but only those who know can see. The seeing is not visual but recognitional — the recognition of the presence that is always there.
